content:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a p99 hop (~30%) on the long-context perf test after the evicter flipped to FIFO during a saturation run. Repro steps and logs below.

Sam: Which job/test? can you paste the metric snapshot?

Alex: perf/long-context-bench (seq=4096, batch=8). Snapshot from /metrics endpoint at the spike: 
```
kv_evictions_total 8421
kv_reinserts_total 4197
kv_pages_in 1283
kv_pages_out 1279
runtime_evicter_sched_ms_p50 12
runtime_evicter_sched_ms_p99 248
request_latency_ms_p99 342
mem_free_bytes 2147483648
```
Looks like a lot of reinserts and scheduler tail latency.

Maya: That p99 on evicter sched is suspicious. We recently changed the fallback policy to FIFO for small-memory arenas when load > 85%. Might be provoking reinsert chains under long contexts. @Sam can you plumb a quick toggle?

Sam: Yes. I pushed a toggle to staging: `eviction.policy_override=none|fifo|lru` in runtime flags. I ran a quick A/B: FIFO (staging-a) vs LRU (staging-b) during the same traffic.

Sam: Results: FIFO p99 request latency 340-360ms, LRU p99 260-280ms. Token throughput roughly same but memory accounted differently (LRU kept hot entries around, FIFO caused more churn).

Dave: Interesting — FIFO helps throughput in some workloads but with long contexts it fragments the KV slab and causes more page-ins. We see page-out/page-in oscillation. Fragmentation -> more CPU on reinsertion -> latency tail.

Alex: I captured a short trace from the runtime profiler (sampling):
```
# flame sample (top frames)
runtime::evicter::process_queue 48%
evict::reinsert_hotpath 22%
kv::alloc_write 12%
kv::page_in 8%
others 10%
```
Evicter is dominating CPU in the tail.

Maya: Two possible fixes: 1) add fast-path guard to avoid FIFO for long-context requests (kernel selection -> prefer LRU when seq_len > N), 2) add an evicter_throttle that batches reinserts and smooths scheduling. Propose we try #2 first (less invasive).

Sam: I added `evicter.throttle_ms = 5` to staging and re-ran. p99 dropped to ~290ms, reinserts/sec dropped 40%. Seems promising.

Dave: Throttle helps but we need correctness guarantees: ensure we don't starve eviction and cause OOM. Can we add a hysteresis: if mem_free < X then bypass throttle?

Maya: Yes — plan: throttle by default, bypass when mem_free_bytes < 1GiB. Also add metric `evicter.throttle_bypassed_total` and an alert if bypass rate > 5% for 5m.

CI-bot: perf/regression-suite #457 finished: long-context-bench FIFO baseline -> p99 345ms; FIFO+throttle -> p99 298ms; LRU baseline -> p99 270ms. No test failures.

Alex: Good. Next steps: (1) ship throttle with hysteresis to canary (eng-runtime/canary), (2) add kernel selection rule to prefer LRU for seq_len > 2048 and re-run perf jobs, (3) add unit test for reinsert-order under FIFO to catch correctness regressions. I'll open the PRs. @Maya can you own the kernel selection rule?

Maya: Yep, will draft the PR today and include microbenchmarks.

Sam: I'll coordinate canary rollout and watch `evicter.*` metrics.

Dave: Also add a short doc in eng-runtime/ops about when FIFO is beneficial vs LRU (operational guidance).

Alex: Thanks all :thumbsup: This looks like the root cause is evicter scheduling + FIFO reinsert churn for long contexts. Throttle + hysteresis is a safe intermediate mitigation; kernel rule is the longer-term fix.

Sam: saving logs and traces to /artifacts/1746504321/ for the postmortem.

Alex: closing this thread — will reference the PR numbers once open.
